This was a rush job to seal off a new opening made in a paper mills sewer system. They have their own water treatment plant designed to handle all the organic & chemical waste released by the cooking, bleaching and further processing of the wood chips bfr making bulk kraft paper. So it had to be resistant to a somewhat caustic environment, thus stainless 316.

So after drafting the parts on the CNC press brake, i started by shearing all the parts, unfortunately the audio doesn't do it justice :

https://hooktube.com/G-kChCLvj3E

Then I traced & punched one of the flanges, the top one to bolt on the cover plate.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104953.jpg

Onto the 60ton Iron Worker to punch the holes. The smaller plates weight 33 lbs & the bigger ones 70lbs, real fun to handle by hand when doing bolt patterns.

https://hooktube.com/NcQ_ZMpPcWg

Then it was time to use the 260ton CNC press brake. It was the first time i used the 3" v-die with the big punch. I have to make adapters for the support arm T-slots to make up the difference in die height from the usual 4 faced v-die.

https://hooktube.com/JTsnvpaMBTw

Putting the box together, 38" × 24". Since this was a rush job we didn't go with a laser cut flange, this meant more welding than should be required.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104960.jpg

That's a big gap to fill on a flange.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104954.jpg

After squaring it up & tacking the flanges flush it was time to weld.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104959.jpg

I used a flux cored wire to weld up this box, I prefer it to mig welding when it comes to thick stainless, no fancy gas mix required & you can go really fast. I used an aluminum bloc as a removable back plate.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104956.jpg

Flux chipped off the first pass

2nd Pass

3 pass cap this made the flange corners flare up & required pressing to correct.

Inside weld

All welded up

After a bit of grinding I marked the cover plate to punch the bolt pattern.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104951.jpg

This cover weighed 98lbs & the engineer (I shit you not, a tranny) called for a single handle.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104949.jpg

Since we had to match a bolt pattern of pre-installed concrete anchors, I drilled the bottom flange.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/5b9eea6e1c/104952.jpg

Austenitic stainless not being magnetic means using a piece of steel to give the magnetic drill a decent footing.
